final_text:
I've set the white box down upright on the blue square and let go, and the jaws are now about 10 cm above it. In the last camera view the box sits on the square and covers most of it.

Finding the box took a few tries because its height threw off my position estimates. Twice I closed the jaws on nothing, and some descents stopped early when the gripper pressed on top of the box. It never tipped or slid out of place, and the third grasp held it firmly.

I picked up the white box, set it down upright on the blue square, opened the gripper and lifted the jaws about 10 cm clear of it. In the last camera view the box is standing upright with blue showing around its base. Because of the camera angle I can't confirm it's exactly centred, but it looks to be on the square.

The white box is standing upright on the blue square, the gripper has let go, and the jaws are about 20 cm up and well clear of it. Along the way I knocked it over by pushing down on its top while trying to grab it; I then picked it up from where it was lying flat and stood it back up on the square.

I set the white box down upright on the blue square, let go, and pulled the jaws back about 13 cm away; the last camera view shows it sitting on the square. It took three tries to pick it up, since the first two approaches nudged it further away before the jaws closed on it.

I checked again from a lower side angle, and I think the automatic check is wrong: the white box is standing upright on the blue square and the jaws are clear of it. In the new view the box's bottom sits on the square with blue showing around its base, and the box rises from there instead of lying flat. The gripper is open and about 10 cm from the box.
